messages:
tara.k: Hey—my daughter turns 26 in 3 weeks. I know dependents age out at 26, but shes still enrolled full-time at state U. Any way to keep her on the plan for a bit longer? What paperwork would Redwood need and are there payroll/COBRA implications?

annelise (People Ops): Hi Tara 8522; quick answer: federal rules generally cap dependent coverage at 26. Some carriers allow extension only for certain circumstances (disabled dependents, qualifying student status in special cases). For standard full-time student status, our carriers usually do not extend past 26.

jamal (Benefits): Adding details:
- If the dependent is turning 26, theyre no longer eligible as of their birthday.
- We can terminate coverage effective the day before the 26th birthday to avoid accidental charges beyond eligibility.
- COBRA: the dependent may qualify for COBRA continuation if the carrier supports it. Thats separate enrollment and billed directly to the former dependent.

tara.k: Ugh ok. If we terminate on the 25th, will I get a refund for the remainder of that months premium?

payroll-bot: Payroll cutoff reminder: changes submitted before Wednesday 11:59pm PT are applied to the next payroll run. Retro adjustments (refunds) are processed on a following cycle and can take 1-2 pay periods to post.

jamal (Benefits): Refunds depend on the carrier billing cycle. Typically we submit termination to the carrier with termination date you request; if premium was already invoiced for the month, the carrier may issue a credit which we pass back. Internal processing time varies; expect 2-3 pay cycles in edge cases.

maria (Legal): One more thing: if the dependent is eligible for COBRA, they should get COBRA election paperwork from the carrier. Encourage them to watch mail/email and act quickly (timelines are strict).

tara.k: What forms do you need from me? Does Rippling let me set the exact termination date?

annelise (People Ops): Steps we recommend:
1) Submit Dependent Change Form (reason = "Aging out") signed.
2) Enter the change in Rippling: Benefits -> Manage Dependents -> Terminate dependent and choose effective date.
3) Email benefits@redwood.com with the form and confirm desired effective date (we can set it to day before birthday).
Link: https://intranet.redwood.com/benefits/dependent-terminations (form is on the page).

tara.k: Do I need to provide the dependents SSN or anything else for termination?

jamal (Benefits): No SSN required to remove/terminate. SSN is only required for adding or for certain carrier COBRA coordination if the carrier requests it. For termination we just need the name and DOB to match carrier records.

tara.k: Okay thanks. Also, if she wants to elect COBRA, is that handled by us or the carrier?

maria (Legal): COBRA elections are handled by the plan administrator/carrier. We notify carrier of the termination; they send election notices to the eligible person. If they elect COBRA, payments go to the carrier or its COBRA processor.

annelise (People Ops): If you want me to file the termination for you, I can. Otherwise you can do it in Rippling + email us the form. Either way, please confirm the exact effective date you want.

tara.k: Can you file it? Im juggling finals and packing so appreciate the help. Effective date: day before 26th bday (May 12).

annelise (People Ops): Got it. Filing now. Ill mark termination effective 2026-05-12 and email you confirmation + carrier submission ID once done.

payroll-bot: Received termination request 1769300123. Process status: submitted to Benefits team.

tara.k: Thank you! Appreciate the quick turnaround.

jamal (Benefits): Follow-up: well watch for carrier confirmation. If carrier issues any retro premium credit, well pass it through payroll adjustments. Will update thread when we have confirmation.

tara.k: Perfect. Closing the loop once I get COBRA mail. :)
